data.narrative:
ClearSpace, a Series A+ space technology company founded by Luc Piguet and Muriel Richard, sits within a competitive landscape of 5 public and 8 private peers in Space & Aerospace. Top private comparables include SpaceX, Sierra Space, Planet Labs, Impulse Space, and Apex Space. Public sector comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) trade at a median 23.9x price-to-sales.

Standard triangulation approaches prove constrained here. Peer-median benchmarking is inapplicable: while 11 same-sector peers exist, zero companies satisfy the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparability, falling below the minimum threshold of 3 datapoints. Public-comp anchoring cannot be executed because ClearSpace's revenue is not on file—standard practice for private companies—making P/S multiple application infeasible. The public sector multiple of 23.9x therefore cannot be reliably translated to a target valuation without disclosed revenue data.

Given the company has raised $36M to date and occupies a highly fragmented subsector with no direct same-stage comps, valuation requires either (1) disclosure of revenue or comparable transaction multiples, or (2) DCF/risk-adjusted return analysis using management guidance. The absence of applicable triangulation methods indicates that conventional relative-value approaches are insufficient here. Primary uncertainties stem from lack of financial transparency and the nascent, heterogeneous nature of the Space & Aerospace private markets.
